title: C# Questions & Answers - Searching and Modifying Strings
sourceFile: Searching & Modifying Strings - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on searching and modification of strings in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which String method is used to extract a substring from a string?
questions.explanation: In C#, the method used to extract a portion of a string is 'Substring()', starting with an uppercase 'S'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The string.Concat() method joins the provided arguments. Here it joins "Ilove", a space " ", and "CSHARP", resulting in "Ilove CSHARP".

questions.question: Which of these methods is used to remove leading and trailing white-space characters in C#?
questions.explanation: The 'Trim()' method in C# removes all leading and trailing white-space characters from the current string.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: TrimStart() removes all leading occurrences of a set of characters. It removes 'I', 'l', and 'o' from "Ilove CSHARP", leaving "ve CSHARP". It stops at 'v' because 'v' is not in the trim list.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The Trim() method removes spaces from both the beginning and the end. The output is wrapped in escaped double quotes.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The '+' operator is used for string concatenation. It joins "Hello" and "Bye" directly without adding any spaces.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: In C#, string.Replace(char, char) replaces all occurrences of the first character with the second character.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the Replace() method?

options.text: Replace() replaces only the last occurrence of a character
Replace() replaces only the first occurrence of a character
Replace() replaces all occurrences of one character with another character

questions.explanation: The Replace() method returns a new string where all instances of a specified Unicode character or String are replaced with another specified character or String.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: Substring(12, 3) starts at index 12 (the space character before 'y') and takes 3 characters, resulting in ' yo'.

questions.question: Which is a correct way to find the index of the second lowercase 's' in a string stored in variable a?
questions.explanation: Find the first match with IndexOf, then search again starting at the next character (i + 1). There is no SecondIndexOf or FirstIndexOf method.
